newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu to attend event despite spat.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu to attend event despite spat.

text.p: Benjamin Netanyahu decided on Thursday to attend a Hebrew University convocation despite a spat with professors who said the Israeli prime minister did not deserve their respect.

The prime minister's spokesman said Netanyahu decided against boycotting the event after the president of the university apologised for the professors' remarks and said they were not speaking on behalf of the institution.
"In light of the president's remarks the prime minister decided to accept his clarification and attend the ceremony at the university as originally planned," the spokesman said in a statement.

The tiff erupted when at least 20 leading professors wrote a letter to the university's president saying Netanyahu was "not worthy of Hebrew University's honour" and declaring their presence at the event should not be perceived as a show of respect for him.

"This prime minister has spent the whole year trying to undermine the fundamental principals of the democratic regime and has acted systematically against free press...(and) against the rule of law," said law professor Mordechai Kremnitzer.

He cited a government corruption scandal involving Netanyahu's ill-fated appointment of an attorney-general in January and other affairs during the year since the right-wing leader formed his government.

Netanyahu has had a rocky relationship with academics and journalists, viewed by some in his rightist Likud party as members of an "establishment elite" that identifies with the opposition Labour party.
"I am not willing to enter a place where I am systematically denigrated," Netanyahu told Israel Radio earlier on Thursday, explaining his decision to cancel the university appearance.
University president Hanoch Gutfreund phoned Netanyahu and asked him to reconsider the decision.
"Those professors...do not speak on behalf of the university," Gutfreund told Israel Radio. "I have always received him (Netanyahu) with respect and have always said his visits are good for us."
